newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian attends suicide of doctor with cancer.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian attends suicide of doctor with cancer.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian attended another suicide on Sunday evening, that of a 71-year-old psychiatrist who was suffering from cancer, Kevorkian's attorney Geoffrey Fieger said.

Fieger told a university lecture audience in Boston that Dr. Richard Faw of Wilson, North Carolina, was pronounced dead at William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak, Michigan, about 7 p.m. EDT (2300 GMT) Sunday. Fieger described Faw as a general practitioner and pyschiatrist whose cancer had spread to other organs.

Yvette Monet, a spokeswoman at the hospital, told Reuters that Dr. Kevorkian dropped off the body of a 71-year-old man at 6 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT). Medical personnel took the body into the hospital and pronounced the man dead.
She also confirmed the deceased was a psychiatrist and general practitioner.
Kevorkian has publicly acknowledged attending 41 deaths, including Sunday's, since he began his assisted-suicide crusade in 1990.
Fieger made the announcement as he began an address on the morality of physician-assisted suicide at a Northeastern University gathering in Boston.

After his speech Fieger told reporters that Faw was screaming in pain and was on morphine. He would not give the exact number of suicides attended by Kevorkian but did say that there have been "between 40 and 80 cases in Michigan."
Fieger would not say where the suicide took place nor what the method of death was.
